items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: And then sometimes I had Art Blakey, you know, if he wasn't doin' nothin'.

ctx.x: Sadik and he worked with you...

At the Paradise, yeah, he stayed with me a long time. I saw Timmie the other night at the Village Vanguard and I...you see I had to change drummers because, you know, all these guys, Gene Ammons, and Bird, and all these guys would come up there and Art Blakey and Max Roach and all these guys, so I had to get a drummer with just a little bit more experience and it broke my heart and I know it hurt him too, you know, but he understood, you know. Yeah.

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: they're still my friends but I said I wasn't goin' to do that

ctx.x: In the '40's there were a number of musicians, I'm sure you knew some of them, who became Muslims. There was a movement that started at that time...

Yes, Art Blake[ey] and Idrees Sulieman and a lot of guys. There was a movement. But I listened to 'em and I says, "Well, I don't feel that I should do that." Just like when the guys start shootin' heroin in their arms, you know, I wasn't, you know, they're still my friends but I said I wasn't goin' to do that. You know what I mean. And that Muslim thing, you know, everyone was excited about it and changin' their names and you'll become a real citizen of America, but it didn't work out like that, you know what I…
